facts.statement: Rutiodon is an extinct genus of phytosaurs that lived during the Late Triassic in the eastern United States.
facts.quote: Rutiodon (meaning "wrinkle tooth") is an extinct genus of mystriosuchine phytosaurs from the Late Triassic of the eastern United States.

facts.statement: The type species, Rutiodon carolinensis, is known from many skulls and postcranial fossils found in the Cumnock Formation of North Carolina.
facts.quote: The type species of Rutiodon, Rutiodon carolinensis, encompasses a large number of skulls and assorted postcranial fossils discovered in the Cumnock Formation of North Carolina.

facts.statement: Fossils of Rutiodon carolinensis have been found in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Virginia.
facts.quote: Fossils referable to the species are also known from Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Virginia.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists recognize a second species, Rutiodon manhattanensis, known from fossils in New Jersey and Pennsylvania.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists also recognize a larger and more robust species, Rutiodon manhattanensis, which is known from teeth and postcranial fossils from New Jersey and Pennsylvania.

facts.statement: Rutiodon resembled a crocodile but had nostrils positioned far back on the head near the eyes rather than at the snout tip.
facts.quote: Like other phytosaurs, Rutiodon strongly resembled a crocodile, but its nostrils were positioned far back on the head, close to the eyes, instead of at the tip of the snout.

facts.statement: Rutiodon possessed enlarged front teeth and a narrow jaw similar to that of a modern gharial.
facts.quote: It had enlarged front teeth, and a relatively narrow jaw, somewhat resembling that of a modern gharial.

facts.statement: Rutiodon likely ate fish and may have also snatched land animals like Coelophysis from the water's edge.
facts.quote: This suggests that this carnivore probably caught fish and it may also have snatched land animals (such as Coelophysis) from the waterside.

facts.statement: Rutiodon was one of the largest carnivores of its time, reaching lengths of up to 8 meters and weighing about 1 metric ton.
facts.quote: Rutiodon was among the largest carnivorous animals of its environment, measuring up to 8 m long and weighing about 1 MT.

facts.statement: Rutiodon carolinensis was originally named by Ebenezer Emmons in 1856 based on fossils from the Deep River coal field in North Carolina.
facts.quote: The type species of Rutiodon is R. carolinensis. It was originally named by Ebenezer Emmons in 1856, based on fossils from the Deep River coal field (Cumnock Formation) of North Carolina.

facts.statement: The largest skull referred to Rutiodon measures 77.3 cm (30.4 inches) in length.
facts.quote: It is also the largest skull referred to Rutiodon, at a length of 77.3 cm (30.4 inches).

facts.statement: A small partial phytosaur skull was discovered in 1963 at the Granton Quarry in North Bergen, New Jersey.
facts.quote: In 1963, a small partial phytosaur skull (AMNH 5500) was discovered at the Granton Quarry of North Bergen, New Jersey.

facts.statement: Fossils tentatively referred to R. carolinensis were unearthed in 1959 in Fairfax County, Virginia, near the construction site of Dulles International Airport.
facts.quote: Phytosaur fossils tentatively referred to R. carolinensis were unearthed in 1959 in Fairfax County, Virginia, near Dulles International Airport which was still under construction.

facts.statement: Fossils of R. manhattanensis were discovered in 1910 in the Stockton Formation near Fort Lee, New Jersey.
facts.quote: Fossils of a second species, R. manhattanensis, were discovered in 1910 from "red sandy marl" (Stockton Formation) below the Palisades near Fort Lee, New Jersey.

facts.statement: R. manhattanensis was described by Friedrich von Huene in 1913, naming it after its proximity to Manhattan.
facts.quote: In 1913, it was described by Friedrich von Huene, who provided a new species name in reference to its close proximity to Manhattan.

facts.statement: R. manhattanensis is differentiated from R. carolinensis by having a proportionally larger tibia and a more robust hip.
facts.quote: It was differentiated from R. carolinensis based on a proportionally larger tibia and more robust hip.

facts.statement: The holotype of R. manhattanensis possesses the largest femur ever observed in phytosaurs, measuring 43-44 cm (17 inches).
facts.quote: Huene remarked that the holotype has the largest femur he had ever observed in phytosaurs, at a length of 43-44 cm (17 inches).

facts.statement: Some authors doubt the validity of R. manhattanensis, suggesting differences between the species may result from sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: A few authors have doubted the validity of R. manhattanensis, arguing that the differences between the two species may be due to sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: Recent studies place Rutiodon in the phytosaur family tree as more derived than Paleorhinus but less derived than Leptosuchus.
facts.quote: Recent papers agree that Rutiodon occupies a tier of the phytosaur family tree more derived than Paleorhinus and less derived than Leptosuchus.

facts.statement: Rutiodon belongs to the clade Phytosauridae (Mystriosuchinae) and is outside the clade Leptosuchomorpha.
facts.quote: In other words, Rutiodon lies within the large clade Phytosauridae (alternatively known as Mystriosuchinae) and outside the less inclusive clade Leptosuchomorpha.

facts.statement: A 2001 abstract proposed that Rutiodon carolinensis was a synonym of Angistorhinus, suggesting Angistorhinus was ancestral to Rutiodon.
facts.quote: A 2001 conference abstract argued that Rutiodon carolinensis was a synonym of Angistorhinus, mirroring older suggestions that Angistorhinus was directly ancestral to Rutiodon.

facts.statement: Rutiodon is classified as an animal in the phylum Chordata, class Sauropsida, order Archosauria, and family Phytosauridae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Sauropsida unranked_ordo: Archosauria ordo: Phytosauria familia: Phytosauridae genus: Rutiodon

facts.statement: Rutiodon, meaning "wrinkle tooth," was an extinct archosaurian saurian of the order Phytosauria that lived during the Triassic period and reached up to 8 meters in length.
facts.quote: Rutiodon ("diente arrugado") es un género extinto de saurópsidos arcosaurios del orden fitosaurios, que vivió en el periodo Triásico, y llegaba a medir hasta 8 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Rutiodon is known from the eastern United States, including North Carolina, New York, and New Jersey.
facts.quote: Rutiodon es conocido del este de Estados Unidos (Carolina del Norte, Nueva York y Nueva Jersey).

facts.statement: Rutiodon resembled a crocodile but had nostrils positioned further back on its head near the eyes rather than at the snout tip.
facts.quote: Como otros fitosaurios, Rutiodon recordaba bastante a un cocodrilo, pero sus narinas estaban posicionadas más atrás en la cabeza, cerca de los ojos, en vez de tenerlas cerca de la punta del hocico.

facts.statement: It possessed elongated front teeth and a relatively narrow jaw similar to that of the modern gharial.
facts.quote: Tenía dientes frontales alargados, y una mandíbula relativamente estrecha, algo similar a la del moderno gavial.

facts.statement: Its back, sides, and tail were covered with bony plates, similar to crocodiles.
facts.quote: Y de la misma forma que en los cocodrilos, su espalda, costados y cola estaban cubiertos con placas óseas.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest this carnivore likely caught fish and may have trapped terrestrial animals near the shores of water bodies.
facts.quote: Esto sugiere que este carnívoro probablemente capturaba peces y pudo haber atrapado animales terrestres en las orillas de cuerpos de agua.

facts.statement: A second species, R. manhattanensis, was discovered in 1910 near Fort Lee and named due to its proximity to Manhattan.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, R. manhattanensis, fue descubierta en 1910 cerca de Fort Lee, y fue nombrada en razón de su proximidad a Manhattan.

facts.statement: Rutiodon belongs to the parent group Mystriosuchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Mystriosuchinae

facts.statement: Rutiodon is classified within the family Parasuchidae.
facts.quote: Family: Parasuchidae

facts.statement: Rutiodon is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Rutiodon lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Rutiodon is one of the best-known phytosaurs and appeared in the 2001 Discovery Channel program When Dinosaurs Roamed America, where it was depicted unsuccessfully attacking a Coelophysis near a riverbank.
facts.quote: Rutiodon es uno de los fitosaurios mejor conocidos y apareció en 2001 en el programa de Discovery Channel When Dinosaurs Roamed America, en el que se lo representaba tratando de atacar a un Coelophysis cerca de la orilla de un río, sin éxito.

rejected.quote: Also, like modern crocodiles, its back, flanks, and tail were covered with bony armored plates.
